Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Asset Management Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, the instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Asset Management's Q3 results. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Investment Officer; Lisa Chen, Head of Distribution; and David Patel, Head of Operations.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by resilient net inflows and favorable market appreciation across our diversified portfolios. Our AUM grew to $1.28 trillion.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Johnathan. From a financial perspective, Apex Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3. Our revenue was $3.72 billion, representing a 22% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by robust management fee expansion and performance fee contributions. Our expenses were $2.30 billion, resulting in net income of $1.10 billion. Our expense ratio improved due to operating leverage and efficiency gains from our digital initiatives.

Good morning, everyone. This is Sarah Jenkins, CFO of Apex Asset Management. I'll dive into our management fee revenue and average fee rate trends for the third quarter, which continue to reflect the resilience of our diversified platform amid a dynamic macro environment. As a reminder, management fees are our core revenue driver, calculated as a percentage of average AUM, and they represented 78% of our total fee revenue this quarter.

Starting with the headline numbers: Q3 management fee revenue came in at $1.28 billion, up 9% year-over-year and 4% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of organic growth in management fees, driven by a combination of 6% AUM market appreciation—primarily from the S&P 500's rally—and $18 billion in net new money, excluding divested legacy mandates. On a constant currency basis, growth was even stronger at 10%, underscoring the benefits of our 45% international AUM mix.

Average fee rate, or AFR, held steady at 44.8 basis points, down just 2 bps sequentially from 45.0 bps in Q2. This stability is notable given persistent industry-wide fee compression, where the broader asset management peer set—think BlackRock, Vanguard, and State Street—saw AFRs decline by an average of 5-7 bps over the past year due to ETF proliferation and passive fund dominance. Our AFR resilience stems from three key pillars: strategic product mix shifts, disciplined pricing, and higher-margin alternative assets.

Let me break it down by asset class. Equities, which comprise 52% of our $1.28 trillion AUM, generated $620 million in fees, up 12% YoY, with an AFR of 48 bps—boosted by strong inflows into our active equity strategies like the Apex Global Equity Partners fund, which outperformed its benchmark by 320 bps over three years. Fixed income, at 28% of AUM, contributed $380 million, flat YoY on an AFR of 35 bps, reflecting some pressure from short-duration bond ETF launches amid Fed rate dynamics. However, our multi-sector credit and emerging market debt sleeves held firm, with net new money of $9 billion offsetting outflows from money market funds as yields normalized.

Alternatives remain our brightest spot: 15% of AUM now, up from 12% a year ago, delivering $210 million in fees—up 22% YoY—at a robust 72 bps AFR. This includes private credit, where we closed $5 billion in commitments to our Apex Private Credit Opportunities fund, mirroring the industry shift toward illiquids as pensions and sovereign wealth funds—like those in the Middle East—seek yield in a higher-for-longer rate world. ETFs and multi-asset solutions rounded out at 5% of AUM, with $70 million in fees but an AFR compression to 18 bps, in line with Vanguard's low-cost index fund dominance.

Regionally, North America drove 65% of fee growth, with $28 billion in net new money from 401(k) rollovers and model portfolio mandates via our RIA channel. EMEA contributed 20%, where our UCITS-compliant ESG equity funds attracted €12 billion amid MiFID II tailwinds and the EU's Sustainable Finance Disclosure Regulation. APAC, now 18% of AUM, saw 15% YoY fee growth to $145 million, fueled by $7 billion in mandates from Japanese GPIFs and Singaporean SWFs into our Asia ex-Japan small-cap strategy—though China exposure remains capped at 5% given regulatory headwinds.

On trends, we've navigated fee compression headwinds effectively. Industry AFRs have fallen from 55 bps in 2019 to around 42 bps today, per Morningstar data, largely from passive equity ETFs capturing 40% market share. At Apex, we've countered this through technical initiatives like our Fee Optimization Engine—a proprietary algo that dynamically tiers fees based on AUM scale, performance hurdles, and client tenure. This preserved 80 bps of margin in our institutional book. We've also accelerated our alternatives build-out, targeting 20% of AUM by 2025 via GP stakes in evergreen funds, similar to Blackstone's model, and co-investment platforms with family offices.

Strategically, we're leaning into higher-conviction active management where alpha persists—our active equity win rate hit 72% in Q3—and embedding ESG across 60% of strategies to tap $40 trillion in sustainable AUM globally, per Bloomberg estimates. We've launched three new interval funds: a private real estate vehicle yielding 9-11% NAV, and two credit-focused ETFs with active overlays to combat pure-passive erosion. M&A remains opportunistic; our $2.5 billion acquisition of a boutique quant shop last year added 150 bps to blended AFR in systematic strategies.

Looking forward, we expect Q4 management fee revenue growth of 7-9% YoY, with AFR stabilizing at 44-45 bps, assuming flat markets and $15-20 billion net new money. Risks include further equity volatility from U.S. election uncertainty or a Fed pivot, but our 55/45 active/passive mix and 30% recurring performance fee exposure position us well. We're committed to returning capital via our $500 million buyback authorization while investing in tech like Aladdin-inspired portfolio analytics to enhance client stickiness.

Turning now to operating margin trends, which continue to reflect the structural resilience of our asset management franchise. Operating margin—defined as adjusted operating income divided by net revenues—remains a key KPI for us, capturing the efficiency of our scalable fee-based model while navigating industry headwinds like fee compression and regulatory costs.

For Q3, our operating margin expanded 410 basis points year-over-year to 38.2%, marking the strongest quarterly reading since Q4 2021. On a trailing 12-month basis, it's now at 37.5%, up from 32.8% a year ago. This performance drove adjusted operating income to $1.42 billion, a 28% increase from Q3 2023, even as net revenues grew 22% on the back of AUM reaching a record $1.28 trillion, up 15% YoY.

The primary tailwind has been operating leverage from AUM growth outpacing expense growth. Our average AUM for the quarter was $1.85 trillion, fueled by 6% net inflows of $112 billion—led by our ETF suite, which captured 12% market share in U.S. equity inflows—and market appreciation, particularly in U.S. large-cap equities and alternatives. Management fees, which comprise 72% of revenues, rose 18% YoY, while performance fees added a $150 million kicker from strong realizations in our private credit and infrastructure strategies.

On the expense side, we grew total operating expenses by just 12% YoY to $2.30 billion, achieving a 10-percentage-point delta versus revenue growth. Compensation and benefits, our largest bucket at 42% of expenses, increased 14% due to variable comp tied to performance and strategic hires in our quant and ESG teams—but we held fixed comp flat through disciplined headcount management, ending the quarter with 14,200 employees, essentially flat YoY. Non-comp expenses rose 10%, moderated by efficiencies in distribution and G&A.

We've leaned heavily into our 'Digital Alpha' initiative, which has delivered over $250 million in annualized run-rate savings since launch in 2022. Key wins include AI-driven portfolio optimization: our proprietary ALPHA platform, now managing 35% of our $450 billion active AUM, has reduced research costs by 22% via machine learning models that automate alpha generation in multi-asset strategies. Robo-advisory scale-up: our digital arm scaled to $180 billion AUM with sub-10 bps operating costs, contributing 250 bps to group margins. Client acquisition costs dropped 15% through targeted digital marketing and API integrations. Cloud migration and outsourcing: we completed 80% migration to AWS for back-office ops, cutting data center costs by 30%, and outsourced non-core custody functions, saving $40 million annually.

These initiatives have boosted our expense-to-revenue ratio to 61.8%, down from 67.2% YoY, positioning us at the higher end of the peer set—ahead of T. Rowe Price's 35-37% range but trailing Vanguard's index-heavy 45%+.

Regionally: Americas (72% of AUM) margins hit 42.5%, up 500 bps YoY, driven by sticky institutional mandates in U.S. equities and private markets. Our $600 billion ETF complex saw 20% flows growth. EMEA (18% of AUM): a softer 32% margin, flat YoY, reflecting MiFID II pressures, offset by UCITS ETF launches with €45 billion in net new money. APAC (10% of AUM): expansion to 28% margins, up 300 bps, on China re-opening tailwinds and Japan equity rallies.

Looking ahead, we see sustained margin tailwinds from alternatives mix-shift—now 28% of AUM with higher fees, targeting $300 billion by 2026; sustainable investing with ESG AUM at $420 billion; and shareholder returns via $2 billion annual buybacks. Risks include fee pressure and comp inflation. We guide FY24 operating margin to 37-39%, with Q4 at ~38.5% assuming stable markets.

Before moving on, some color on the key drivers behind our AUM, which ended Q3 at $1.28 trillion, up 8% quarter-over-quarter and strong year-over-year. AUM directly influences fee-related earnings. Market performance contributed $105 billion, or 74% of the increase, driven by the S&P 500's rally. Our equity strategies (55% of AUM) added $65 billion; thematic ETFs like AI & Semiconductors surged 18%. Fixed income (25%) added $18 billion; alternatives $15 billion at 3.5% appreciation.

Net flows posted $38 billion organic inflows, 2.7% growth, above peers. YTD $112 billion with 95% retention. Retail $22 billion led by ETFs; institutional $16 billion from major wins. Americas 65% of flows; EMEA $8 billion; APAC standout at $5 billion.

These dynamics highlight our hybrid model and tech like Apex Digital Wealth. We project Q4 AUM growth of 4-6%.

Finally, on total net flows: Q3 came in at $18 billion, our strongest in recent quarters, building on YTD strength. Gross inflows $28.6 billion against outflows $16.2 billion, 1.76x ratio. ETFs led with strong demand; alternatives $3.8 billion; equities and fixed income resilient.

By channel: institutional $6.8 billion; retail/wealth $5.6 billion. Regionally balanced: Americas $8.1 billion; EMEA $2.9 billion; APAC $1.4 billion. Full-year on track for robust growth, validating our playbook of innovation, tech, and ESG.

Michael Torres: Thank you, Sarah. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We are navigating the current market environment by maintaining a balanced beta exposure of 1.1x to equities and 0.8x to fixed income, while leaning into AI-themed and private credit opportunities. We launched the Apex AI & Robotics ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $2.5 billion gathered since July and strong outperformance versus benchmarks.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Michael. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in APAC are paying off, as evidenced by 30% YoY growth, $10-12 billion projected flows from Hong Kong and Australian super funds into China A-shares strategies.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've made significant progress in improving our technology infrastructure, including $200 million in ApexFlow analytics for flow forecasting accuracy within ±5% via machine learning. This has resulted in increased efficiency and reduced operational risk. We are also focused on cloud migrations and outsourcing to drive further savings.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, David. In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes targeting mid-to-high single-digit organic AUM expansion through fiscal 2025, reaching $1.6 trillion by year-end—a 9% CAGR. Equities at 45% of AUM saw strong flows; fixed income and alts resilient; ETFs grew 18% YoY. Organic net flows $90-110 billion for FY24, driven by product innovation like three new thematic ETFs, VistaForge tech platform boosting retention to 97%, and regional strength: U.S. $50-60 billion, Europe $25-30 billion, APAC 15-20% CAGR. Inorganic tuck-ins and client wallet share gains position us for top-quartile growth, with risks like high rates mitigated by diversification.

Before we open the line for Q&A, Sarah, some detailed forward guidance on AUM and flows. We closed Q3 with record AUM of $1.28 trillion, up 8% QoQ, driven by $18 billion net inflows and 120 bps market beta. Long-term organic growth 7.2% annualized, outpacing peers.

For Q4, net inflows $22-27 billion: retail/wealth $12-15 billion from ETFs and ESG; institutional $8-10 billion in alts/LDI; HNW/SMAs $2-3 billion. AUM $1.35-1.38 trillion assuming +3-5% markets, with AFR up 20 bps to 42 bps.

FY24: $85-100 billion inflows, year-end AUM $1.50-1.55 trillion, 12-15% organic growth. Product momentum: equities $40-45 billion on AI; FI $25-30 billion; alts $25 billion. Regional: Americas $60-70 billion; EMEA $15-20 billion; APAC $10-12 billion. Digitization via ApexFlow, M&A tuck-ins, 15% cash allocation. Risks: inflation or China landing; upside from volatility.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning, everyone. As we wrap up our Q3 results, our total AUM stood at $1.42 trillion adjusted for guidance, reflecting 12% YoY and 4% QoQ growth from $28 billion inflows and S&P rally. Segments: equities $639 billion; FI $426 billion; alts $213 billion; ETFs $285 billion; ESG $142 billion up 22%.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Johnson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the AUM and flow guidance for upcoming periods?

Johnathan Hale: Good question, Mike. As Sarah outlined, we're guiding Q4 net inflows to $22-27 billion, accelerating from Q3, with AUM to $1.35-1.38 trillion. FY24 full-year $85-100 billion inflows for $1.50-1.55 trillion end AUM. This is driven by channel strength and product momentum, with risks balanced by our diversified positioning.

Mike Johnson: Thank you. And a follow-up on trends in operating margin?

Sarah Jenkins: Absolutely, Mike. Our Q3 margin hit 38.2%, up 410 bps YoY from leverage and Digital Alpha savings—$250 million run-rate. Tech like ALPHA cut research 22%; robo at sub-10 bps costs. Guide FY24 37-39%. Alternatives shift and ESG premiums support further expansion.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the Apex Global Equity Partners fund?

Michael Torres: Thanks, Emily. The fund delivered 320 bps outperformance over three years, with Q3 returns of 11.5% net amid S&P strength. Our active overlays captured AI rotation effectively, maintaining 72% win rate versus benchmarks.

Emily Carter: And how is the new product Apex AI & Robotics ETF performing relative to expectations?

Lisa Chen: Early traction exceeds expectations, Emily—with $2.5 billion inflows since July on 25% YTD gains in semis. Retail demand via RIAs is robust, mirroring ARK/Global X success, positioning for $500 million seed acceleration.

Operator: Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel: Can you provide more color on the operational efficiencies you've gained?

David Patel: Sure, Raj. Our ApexFlow investment enhances forecasting to ±5%; AWS migration saved 30% on data centers; outsourcing custody $40 million annually. Onboarding friction down 40% via APIs, boosting efficiency and reducing risk across 14,200 employees.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
